item.text: {"analysis":"Trial completed successfully and passed host predictor evaluation. Authoritative macro validation HR@10 was 0.565: Movies_and_TV 0.615, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.620, Electronics 0.430, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.595. Allocated GPU time was 424.57 seconds. Electronics was the weakest category. The result confirms executable training and export, but does not establish that R-Drop or bidirectional masking improves performance; no controlled ablation is provided. Corrupted patch fragments remain inert inside multiline strings, while the active forward pass and export check execute successfully.","code_summary":"One independently trained masked SASRec model per category, with exactly one selected checkpoint loaded for prediction. Architecture: 96-dimensional tied item embeddings, learned positions, two bidirectional pre-normalized Transformer blocks, two attention heads, GELU output projection, dropout 0.2, and jointly learned item biases; no relative attention bias. Training masks the final item and 20% of context positions, uses sampled cross-entropy with 256 shared negatives, and applies symmetric KL regularization of weight 0.1 across two dropout passes of the same network. Final-position and auxiliary losses receive equal weight. AdamW uses learning rate 0.0006; training seed is 42. Checkpoints are selected by local validation HR@10 with NDCG tie-breaking. The generated predictor preserves four-category routing and appends a final query mask; export checks compare its scores against direct model inference."}
